simple.meaning: כְּנָת (kᵉnâth) is a Hebrew word meaning “a colleague (as having the same title).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: כְּנָת (H3674) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 4:7, with occurrences in Ezra.

definitions.short: a colleague (as having the same title)
definitions.full: H3674. kenath [ כְּנָת ] noun [of men, but feminine in form, Ges § 122 , 4. b] associate, colleague (loan-word from Biblical Aramaic כְּנָת ; Syriac , compare also Schw Idioticon 46 ; on formative see Lag BN 82 ); — only Aram plural כְּנָוֺתָו֯ שְׁאָר Ezra 4:7 the rest of his associates.

occurrences.englishText: In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his companions, wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the writing of the letter was written in Syrian, and delivered in the Syrian language.
